data.title: Shanghai RAAS to Take Over Boehringer Ingelheim China Unit for Up to USD3 Million
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- Shanghai RAAS Blood Products will acquire 100 percent of the shares of German drugmaker Boehringer Ingelheim's biopharmaceuticals unit in China for no more than CNY20 million (USD3 million) in cash, the leading Chinese blood products company said yesterday, citing the agreement signed by both parties that day.

The takeover comes as Shanghai RAAS looks to innovative drugs as its second growth engine amid falling profits across China’s blood products industry since 2025.

The firm is focusing on developing multiple antibody drugs featuring potentially first-in-class new targets and mechanisms in fields including coagulation, autoimmune diseases and inflammation, it said.

Among these is Shanghai RAAS' SR604 injection, the world's first monoclonal antibody targeting activated protein C for the treatment of hemophilia. Its indications for hemophilia A and B have entered Phase III clinical trials.

Boehringer Ingelheim Biopharmaceuticals (China), which is the German firm's biopharmaceutical manufacturing base in Shanghai’s Zhangjiang hi-tech area, has undertaken the technology transfer, process scale-up and production of clinical trial samples for the Phase II and III studies of SR604.

For Ingelheim-based Boehringer Ingelheim, competition in China’s contract development and manufacturing organization sector is intense, with leading players such as WuXi Biologics holding a significant advantage.

Boehringer Ingelheim Biopharmaceuticals (China), which was established in 2014, made a net loss of CNY16.7 million (USD2.5 million) in the first three months on operating revenue of CNY32.5 million (USD4.8 million). Last year it racked up a net loss of CNY259 million (USD38.5 million) on revenue of CNY232 million and in 2024 it had a net loss of CNY73.3 million on operating revenue of CNY586 million (USD87.3 million).

China’s blood products industry has broadly exhibited a "rising revenue but falling profit" trend since 2025. Most companies have continued to see growth in revenue and plasma collection volumes, but profits have generally declined significantly.

Shanghai RAAS’ net profit plunged 35.8 percent in the first half from a year ago to CNY660 million (USD98.3 million), while its operating revenue slumped 18.8 percent to CNY3.2 billion (USD478 million).

Shanghai RAAS’s share price [SHE: 002252] climbed 1 percent today to end the day at CNY5.02 (USD0.75).

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Tesla Offers Up to USD1,940 Incentive to Chinese Buyers Amid September Discount Rush
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 7 -- US electric vehicle giant Tesla has joined a new round of price cuts in China's auto market, offering buyers temporary subsidies of up to CNY13,000 (USD1,940) that bring purchase costs to record lows.

Buyers who order and take delivery of Model 3 and Model Y vehicles by Sept. 30 can receive cash rewards of CNY5,000 and CNY10,000 (USD745 and USD1,490), respectively, while buyers of designated Model 3 versions can get an additional CNY8,000 insurance subsidy, Tesla China announced today.

After the incentives, the lowest prices of the Model 3 and Model Y in China have fallen to CNY222,500 and CNY253,500 (USD33,150 and USD37,770), respectively, their lowest since the refreshed versions of the two models were launched, Tesla noted.

The move comes as more than 10 automakers have rolled out promotions in China since the start of September, including options packages, cash subsidies, and preferential financing, amid sluggish demand in the world's largest auto market.

Electric vehicle maker Leapmotor Technology, for example, launched purchase benefits worth up to CNY19,680 on Sept. 1, including complimentary interior and exterior options and charging stations. Geely Auto-backed Zeekr recently offered a CNY10,000 insurance subsidy as well as financing and options discounts for its flagship Zeekr 8X sports utility vehicle.

Luxury gasoline-powered car brands have introduced even steeper discounts. SAIC Audi recently announced limited-time September prices of CNY262,800 for its A7L luxury four-door coupe and CNY467,600 for its Q6 SUV -- discounts of 37 percent and 29 percent respectively off their official guide prices.

The latest round of price cuts comes against a backdrop of weakness in China's auto market this year. Retail sales of passenger cars fell 20 percent from a year earlier to 11.8 million units in the first eight months, while retail sales of new energy vehicles dropped 11 percent to 6.7 million units, according to the latest data from the China Passenger Car Association.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s Sanxing Hits Limit-Up on Bagging USD132 Million Equipment Deal for US Data Center
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- Shares in Sanxing Medical Electric soared by the daily trading limit today after the Chinese supplier of smart meters and other power equipment said that a subsidiary has won a USD132 million contract to supply transformer equipment for the energy storage system of a data center in the United States.

Sanxing Medical’s share price [SHA:601567] surged 10 percent to reach CNY16.25 (USD2.42).

AUX Smart Technology has secured a contract to supply oil-immersed transformers for an energy storage system at a US data center, Sanxing Medical said yesterday.

The contract value represents 6.1 percent of the Ningbo-based company's audited operating revenue in the fiscal year 2025 and is expected to have a positive impact on its financial performance, the firm said, without disclosing any further details such as the name of the customer, transformer specifications, supply volumes or the delivery schedule.

The contract marks an important breakthrough in Sanxing Medical’s efforts to tap the US data center market, it said. It will help the company further expand its overseas business footprint and enhance its competitive advantage in international markets.

Sanxing Medical's oil-immersed transformers are primarily used in grid distribution, industrial applications, renewable energy and infrastructure. In March, the firm secured a total of EUR117 million (USD133 million) in orders from Dutch distribution network operator Enexis Netbeheer, marking its first breakthrough in the high-end power distribution equipment market in Western Europe. In June, it won another order of EUR13.7 million (USD15.6 million) from Finnish power utility Caruna.

Rapid growth in demand for artificial intelligence computing power has fueled a global data center construction boom, boosting demand for related equipment. Another firm, Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group, which is a supplier of equipment for the oil and gas industry, has signed five contracts to supply gas turbine generator sets to several US data centers since November 2025, with a total order value of USD2.2 billion.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China’s iQIYI Bets on AI, Decentralized Ecosystem to Drive Growth
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- iQIYI is going "all in on AI" and building a decentralized ecosystem as part of two major strategic priorities aimed at lowering content costs, while boosting revenue quality and profitability, the details of which were laid out at the Chinese video-streaming giant’s iJOY Autumn Conference in Shanghai yesterday.

"Traditional film and television content is simply too expensive," said Gong Yu, iQIYI's founder and chief executive officer. "A single movie or TV series can cost tens of millions of Chinese yuan, equivalent to millions of US dollars, at the very least, and up to several hundred million yuan."

Artificial intelligence is already being adopted extensively across film and TV production, improving the viewing experience while shortening production cycles and reducing costs, he said. Citing the economic concept known as the Jevons paradox, Gong argued that if the cost of producing each minute of content falls by an order of magnitude, the number of creators could rise 10-fold and the number of works 100-fold, ultimately driving a sharp increase in consumption.

Based on this outlook, iQIYI is repositioning itself. Gong said the Beijing-based firm is moving away from a "centralized media" model, in which the platform takes the lead in acquiring, producing and marketing content, toward a "decentralized" ecosystem that connects creators directly with audiences.

Gong said he expects the long-form video industry as a whole to follow the same path. In his view, many capable creators no longer need extensive involvement from platforms and can directly upload long-form works. In the future, long-form video and film could increasingly adopt a social media model, similar to platforms such as Weibo, Douyin, which is the Chinese version of TikTok, and Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote, he added.

To this end, iQIYI has built seven major creator support systems, including its creator hub the iQIYI Creator Center, NadouPro, which is a production workflow platform powered by large language models, offline creative centers as well as venture summits. iQIYI said its goal is to help creators "get seen, get paid and get recognized."

The platform now offers more than 6,600 IP titles and 1,600 digital assets, as well as a newly launched script marketplace, iQIYI said yesterday. iQIYI also said in July that the iQIYI Creator Center had added hundreds of thousands of creators since its April revamp, including short-video creators. More than 50,000 micro-dramas and nearly 30,000 micro-animations are now available on the platform.

Revenue-Sharing Model

Under iQIYI’s revenue-sharing rules announced in August, creators are paid a percentage of the revenue the platform attributes to their works. Creators of exclusive short dramas, including AI-generated ones, can receive 100 percent of that revenue. The rate for mid-length dramas without upfront guarantees rises on a tiered basis to as much as 130 percent.

Two AI-generated internet films released in August recouped their production costs within the first week, iQIYI said. Their combined revenue-sharing earnings from box office proceeds topped CNY8 million (USD1.1 million) in the first month. So far this year, iQIYI has released 16 AI-generated micro-dramas under its revenue-sharing model.

However, iQIYI Chief Content Officer Wang Xiaohui said during the company's second-quarter earnings call that long-form dramas and theatrical films will continue to rely mainly on live-action production, with AI being used to help cut costs.

At the event, iQIYI unveiled a slate of more than 350 new titles for 2026 and 2027. The company also released the trailer for its first full-length hybrid AI multi-season drama, "Immortals Over Mortal Love," which combines AI-generated content with live-action performances by professional actors. A period drama combining live-action performances with AI-generated content is scheduled for release next year.

New Growth Areas

On monetization, iQIYI sees advertising on large-screen devices as a new growth area. The proportion of viewing time on iQIYI’s TV platform increased to 50.58 percent in the first half, up from 42.85 percent in 2022, Gong said. However, he said the marketing value of internet-connected TVs has long been underestimated.

iQIYI has launched Baitai Qiantong, a big-data marketing system for household devices. The system can use data from members and multiple devices to identify long-term needs and preferences both at the household and broader group level.

In the second quarter, iQIYI’s non-GAAP operating loss narrowed 12.3 percent from the previous quarter to CNY130.3 million (USD18.2 million) while total revenue climbed 1 percent to CNY6.3 billion (USD880 million).

Its international business has continued to grow rapidly. Membership revenue from iQIYI's overseas service soared 40 percent in the second quarter from a year earlier. Membership revenue in Brazil surged more than 215 percent and in Mexico it jumped more than 150 percent, while Arabic-speaking markets expanded 85 percent.

Micro-dramas have become the company’s second-largest source of overseas membership revenue, with revenue from the category more than quadrupling in the second quarter from a year earlier. The firm said it is already using AI for translation and to localize and distribute overseas content, as well as to produce AI-generated micro-dramas.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Chinese Brands Need Culture to Escape Low-Price Image, Broadcaster Yang Lan Says at London Art Show
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- Chinese companies should tap culture and design to build stronger brands and command higher prices overseas, according to prominent broadcaster and entrepreneur Yang Lan, who is co-curating a Chinese craft and design exhibition in London.

“We must look to culture to build brand value,” Yang, chairperson of Sun Media Group, told Yicai in London. Chinese products risk remaining associated with low prices when overseas consumers judge their value mainly by materials and manufacturing costs, she added.

Yang is one of China's best-known television hosts. She rose to fame in the 1990s presenting Zhengda Variety Show on state broadcaster CCTV, and later interviewed world leaders and business figures on her long-running talk show Yang Lan One on One. She also co-founded Sun Media Group, a private media company, and represented Beijing in its successful bid to host the 2008 Olympic Games.

That push to turn culture into brand value is at the heart of Yang’s latest international project. She co-curated Reviving Craft: Reflection of the Mind with Su Dan, a professor at Tsinghua University’s Academy of Arts & Design. The touring exhibition’s latest edition is running at Somerset House in London until Sept. 27 as an official special project partner of the 2026 London Design Festival.

The free exhibition features more than 70 artists and designers and over 150 works spanning traditional craftsmanship and contemporary design, according to the organizers. It follows editions at the Musée des Arts Décoratifs in Paris in 2024 and Palazzo Serbelloni in Milan last year.

Changing Perceptions of Chinese Brands

For Yang, the commercial challenge is to change how Chinese products are perceived overseas.

Some international audiences still associate Chinese craftsmanship mainly with antiques, while modern Chinese manufacturing has long been linked with low-cost mass production, she said. Exhibitions can help introduce them to a new generation of Chinese makers and designers.

Chinese businesses participating in the project -- spanning new energy vehicles, consumer electronics, furniture, baijiu, and tea -- are increasingly working with artists and designers and drawing on their cultural roots to develop more compelling brand stories, Yang said.

“Our cultural and industrial expansion overseas go hand in hand and reinforce one another,” she said.

Yang ultimately wants to turn Reviving Craft into a leading international platform for Chinese traditional craftsmanship and contemporary design, connecting creators with the global art market through exhibitions, auctions, collector sales, and co-branded projects.

That commercial connection is already beginning to take shape. Some works in the London exhibition have been reserved for purchase by collectors after the show closes, Yang said. Such purchases provide tangible recognition of the makers’ work while allowing designers to benefit directly, she added.

From Exhibition to Global Platform

Gaining access to established international art and design venues has been another part of that effort. Yang said the team set out to exhibit in major design capitals and their cultural landmarks, seeking recognition from professional institutions as well as the wider public.

The project is also developing ties with the Queen Elizabeth Scholarship Trust, a British charity that supports training in craftsmanship. Yang said the cooperation is intended to help art and design students in the United Kingdom travel to China to learn directly from traditional craft practitioners, with proceeds from a charity auction held during the London event supporting the initiative.

She sees such training as a way to build lasting connections beyond individual exhibitions, with scope for exchanges drawing on the craft traditions of both countries.

Reviving Craft will continue exploring new markets while deepening its presence in places it has already visited, Yang said. Cooperation with industry can provide sustained support for artistic work, while exhibitions can help designers gain international visibility and reach potential buyers.

“Through exhibitions, auctions, collecting, sales and co-branded collaborations, we want to bring art and the market together,” she said.

data.title: Chinese Cancer Drug Developer InnoCare, Eli Lilly Ink Deal Worth up to USD3.35 Billion
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- China's InnoCare Pharma has signed a research collaboration and licensing agreement with American pharma giant Eli Lilly and Co. to discover innovative drugs, with the Chinese drug developer eligible for payments of up to USD3.35 billion.

Under the agreement, InnoCare is eligible to receive up to USD100 million in upfront and near-term milestone payments and about USD3.25 billion in potential development and commercial milestone payments, the Beijing-based company said in a statement today.

Founded in 2015, InnoCare is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing innovative treatments for cancer and autoimmune diseases. Its key product is orelabrutinib, a Bruton’s tyrosine kinase inhibitor approved in China and Singapore for certain blood cancers.

InnoCare said the latest agreement marks an important milestone in its internationalization strategy and is expected to enhance its global competitiveness and influence, and have a positive impact on its future performance.

Based on the deal, InnoCare will use its proprietary drug discovery platform and research and development expertise to discover and advance compounds against up to five novel targets to address major unmet medical needs. The firm will also be entitled to tiered royalties at single-digit percentages based on annual net sales of licensed products following their commercialization.

The Lilly agreement follows another major overseas licensing deal by InnoCare. In October last year, the company granted Nasdaq-listed Zenas BioPharma global rights to orelabrutinib for multiple sclerosis and rights outside China and Southeast Asia for other non-oncology indications, along with rights to two preclinical autoimmune drug candidates.

The Zenas partnership had a smaller potential value than the Lilly deal. InnoCare was eligible for up to USD100 million in upfront and near-term payments, up to seven million Zenas shares, and additional milestone payments and royalties. Potential payments across the three programs exceeded USD2 billion.

The new licensing deal failed to lift InnoCare's shares amid a broader market selloff. InnoCare [SHA: 688428; HK: 09969] closed 10.6 percent lower at CNY29.86 (USD4.50) in Shanghai today and slipped 7.9 percent to HKD14.50 (USD1.90) in Hong Kong.

Chinese stocks came under selling pressure after the 10-year US Treasury yield hit a 19-year high yesterday, with the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index closing 1.2 percent lower today.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Shanghai Used Home Prices Jump as Lower-Cost Listings Thin Out
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- Second-hand home prices have risen noticeably in several parts of Shanghai since the start of the year, with gains of as much as 20 percent in some neighborhoods, as the supply of lower-priced properties dries up, according to local property market professionals.

The near-disappearance of lower-priced listings has been one of the most notable changes in the city's pre-owned housing market, Zhang Shaojun, head of a branch of property realtor Lianjia near Shanghai's East Bund in northeast Yangpu district, told Yicai.

Prices in the area hit their low point between late last year and early this year, Zhang said, adding that they began a slow recovery after the Chinese New Year holiday, and the upward trend has become more pronounced this quarter.

Prices for some older apartments in the area have climbed to more than CNY45,000 (USD6,700) per square meter from about CNY35,000 to CNY40,000 (USD5,210 to USD5,960) per sqm at the start of 2026, Zhang noted. Prices for some relatively new homes have also risen to about CNY90,000 per sqm from early-year lows of around CNY80,000 per sqm.

“This is a broad-based increase,” he said. “Transaction prices for older apartments, near-new homes, and properties along subway lines in the area

have all gone up, with gains ranging from roughly 8 percent to 20 percent.”

Among recent second-hand homebuyers in the area, Zhang has also seen an increase in people working in sectors such as software and finance. Most are aged between 35 and 45 and are mainly buying homes to upgrade their living conditions.

A similar trend has emerged around Shanghai West Railway Station in northwest Putuo district, according to Shi Bing, head of Lianjia's flagship store for the area. Prices in this area bottomed out early this year, and have increased since March and particularly since July, Shi said.

“July is typically a slow season for the second-hand housing market, but viewing activity and transactions were far stronger than expected,” he noted.

The area around the station is characterized by properties built in the 1980s and 1990s and has long been regarded as one of the lower-priced areas in Shanghai's central urban districts.

Fewer Listings

At the start of the year, a typical older apartment in this area -- around 50 sqm, on a middle floor, and without an elevator -- sold for about CNY1.8 million to CNY1.9 million (USD268,000 to USD283,000), Shi said. That has risen to between CNY2 million and CNY2.2 million, with the price per sqm climbing from about CNY35,000 to CNY38,000 to over CNY40,000.

Shi said higher viewings and transactions has rapidly reduced the number of homes available for sale in some communities. Previously, a typical complex may have had more than 40 listings. That is now down to around 15, so buyers have fewer and fewer options, he said.

“It used to be a case of houses looking for buyers,” Shi said. “Now it is a case of buyers looking for houses.” As a result, his team's focus has shifted toward finding more listings.

In addition to these two areas, five other subareas in the city center have also seen notable increases in used home prices, according to a representative for Lianjia Shanghai.

Prices for pre-owned residential properties in Shanghai edged up 0.2 percent in February from January and have increased every month since then through August, according to the latest official figures.

Zhang attributes the recovery to the combined effects of policy support, demand, the composition of available housing stock, and changes in market expectations. The effects of real estate stimulus policies across China are gradually becoming apparent, according to Zhu Jin, chief analyst for real estate, construction, and REITs at CSC Financial.

As Shanghai’s market stabilizes, the used home markets in Shenzhen, Beijing, and Guangzhou are highly likely to follow suit, Zhu said. He expects the recovery in leading cities to gradually spread to other markets, although the pace and magnitude of the rebound in top-tier cities such as Shanghai are likely to continue outstripping the national average.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: China’s CAS Space Sends AI Computing Power Satellite Into Space
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 21 -- CAS Space Technology, a commercial space firm incubated by the Chinese Academy of Sciences, has launched into orbit an artificial intelligence computing power satellite capable of processing acquired information in real time to explore the deployment of computing power infrastructure in space.

The Lijian-1 Y18 carrier rocket launched yesterday from the Dongfeng Commercial Space Innovation Test Zone at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in Northwest China, sending S· AIDC-1 and eight other satellites for space environment monitoring, disaster prevention and mitigation, and scientific experiments into their designated orbits, Guangzhou-based CAS Space announced yesterday.

Developed by Chinese computing power provider S· AIDC, S· AIDC-1 carried a remote sensing camera and an AI computer. It features optical remote sensing imaging, in-orbit data processing, and target recognition capabilities intended for applications in smart cities, natural resource surveys and supervision, precision agriculture, ecological environmental protection, and emergency disaster relief.

Compared with traditional remote sensing satellites, S· AIDC-1 can perform image analysis and target identification in space and then transmit processed, high-value information to the ground, reducing data response times from hours to minutes, according to CAS Space.

The launch was the 17th of the Lijian carrier rocket series, which has sent one spacecraft and 121 satellites into space so far, with a total payload mass exceeding 21 tons. The Lijian series has many orders on hand, with launches planned for the second half of next year.

CAS Space is the private Chinese commercial space company that launched the most satellites and carried the heaviest payload, the company noted, adding that it will complete Lijian-1’s first maritime launch soon, forming a coordinated land-sea launch service capability.

Coordinated sea-land launch services can broaden mission adaptation boundaries and respond efficiently to diverse commercial space needs, including constellation networking, CAS Space said. In the future, the company will collaborate with partners in AI, biomedicine, and other fields to explore more ways to integrate commercial aerospace with emerging industries.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s LB Group to Take Control of Australian Mineral Sands Projects in USD113 Million Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- China’s LB Group said the global leading supplier of titanium dioxide plans to acquire control of two mineral sands projects in Western Australia for AUD160 million (USD113 million) in a move aimed at strengthening its access to raw materials.

LB Group or a subsidiary will buy an 80 percent stake in the Durack and Yandanooka mineral sands projects from Titon Resources, a unit of Australia’s Image Resources, in a cash and assets deal, the Jiaozuo-based company announced late yesterday after signing an exclusive letter of intent.

The deal will help LB secure a stable, long-term supply of raw materials for its titanium dioxide and zirconium businesses, while strengthening its resource security and core competitiveness, it pointed out.

The transaction comprises about AUD20 million (USD14.1 million) in cash and about AUD140 million worth of machinery, equipment, and other assets valued by agreement between the parties, according to LB.

Both projects are located in the North Perth Basin, about 300 kilometers north of Perth, and are intended to produce heavy mineral concentrate through mining and processing, with zircon and titanium-bearing minerals -- including ilmenite, rutile, and leucoxene -- among the main valuable minerals. They have exploration licenses but have yet to obtain mining permits or begin mining operations.

Under the JORC 2012 reporting standard, Durack has 37.7 million tons of mineral resources at a total heavy-mineral grade of 2.2 percent, LB said. Yandanooka has 57 million tons at a 3.1 percent grade.

The acquisition constitutes a related-party transaction because LB indirectly holds a combined 22.6 percent stake in Image Resources through two subsidiaries, making it that firm’s largest shareholder. Xu Ran, LB's controlling shareholder and chairwoman, is also a director of Image Resources, according to the announcement.

The parties will consider relevant factors and negotiate the specific investment structure for the deal, such as a direct acquisition of shares in the project company or the establishment of an unincorporated joint venture for the projects. Through negotiation, the parties will decide the final number for the size of the deal and the exact ownership ratios.

The transaction remains subject to due diligence and valuation, signing, and approval by each companies' shareholders and Australian regulators, including the Foreign Investment Review Board, LB noted.

LB’s shares [SHE: 002601] closed down 1.6 percent at CNY15.00 (USD2.24) each in Shenzhen today after rising as much as 1 percent earlier. Pressured by the marked rise in US Treasury yields overnight, China’s stock market faced heavy selling pressure today. The benchmark Shenzhen Component Index fell 2.3 percent at the close.


Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: China’s Zijin Longking to Invest USD232 Million in Solar-Storage Projects at South American Gold Mines
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- China’s Zijin Longking will invest USD232 million to expand green energy infrastructure at two gold mines in South America operated by its major shareholder, replacing a greater share of expensive diesel generation with solar power and battery storage to lower operating costs, improve energy security, and support mine expansion.

USD150 million will go on the second phase of a solar-plus-storage project at the Rosebel gold mine in Suriname, USD55 million on a new project for the underground mining area of Guyana’s Aurora gold mine, and about USD26.6 million for the third stage of a project for Aurora’s concentrator plant, Longyan-based Zijin Longking announced late yesterday.

The electricity produced by all three projects will be used exclusively at the mines, according to the Zijin Mining Group-controlled company, which supplies air pollution control equipment and develops new energy power projects.

Zijin Longking’s shares [SHA: 600388] finished 1.4 percent higher at CNY17.46 (USD2.6) each today. The broader Shanghai market lost 1.2 percent.

The second phase of the project at Rosebel is expected to generate about 244 million kilowatt-hours of electricity per year and is scheduled for commissioning in the third quarter of next year. At Aurora, the project is expected to generate about 61.8 million kWh annually, while the concentrator plant’s third phase project is forecast to produce roughly 20.6 million kWh per year. Both Guyana projects are targeted for completion during the fourth quarter of next year.

The company has already deployed solar-plus-storage facilities at both mining operations, including a first-stage project at Rosebel and first- and second-stage projects at Aurora’s concentrator plant. As the scale of mining and processing expands, power demand is expected to climb, necessitating the addition of larger-scale clean energy facilities, the company said.

Both the Rosebel and Aurora mines have long depended on diesel power generation, with costs fluctuating sharply in response to changes in international oil prices. Once completed and operational, the projects will slash electricity costs for mining operations and drive the transformation of the local energy mix, the firm said.

The two gold mines involved are both controlled and operated by Zijin Gold International, a subsidiary of Zijin Mining Group.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: China’s Linglong Tyre Plans USD270 Million Investment in New Egyptian Plant
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- Linglong Tyre plans to expand its global manufacturing footprint by investing USD270 million in a new tire factory in Egypt, which will serve as an export hub for Europe, the Middle East, and Africa while reducing trade-related risks and fortifying the Chinese firm's international supply chain.

Linglong Tyre will set up a wholly-owned subsidiary in Egypt to oversee the new plant’s construction and operation, the Shandong province-based firm announced yesterday. The factory will be able to make 6 million semi-steel radial tires a year, with management projecting annual revenue of USD173 million and net profit of USD34.6 million. Construction will take two years.

Financing for the project will come mainly from the company's own capital and bank loans, it said, adding that the plan is subject to the completion of all required approval and filing procedures with the authorities in China and Egypt.

By locating the project in the north African country, Linglong Tyre aims to establish a manufacturing and distribution platform that can serve not only the local market but also clients across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. The facility is expected to work closely with the company's existing overseas plants, improving regional order fulfillment and delivery efficiency.

Management expects the project to help reduce Linglong Tyre's exposure to trade restrictions, while supporting the company’s global expansion strategy and strengthening its long-term competitiveness.

Linglong Tyre, a large specialized tiremaker, has eight research and development centers and seven production bases worldwide, employing over 17,000 people. Its products are widely used in passenger and commercial vehicles as well as in other machinery.

Shares of Linglong Tyre [SHA: 601966] closed 1.3 percent lower at CNY10.41 (USD1.55) each today. The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index gave up 1.2 percent.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: FutureChina Global Forum Adds New AI Track to Explore AI’s Promise and Risks
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24 -- The 17th FutureChina Global Forum opens in Singapore today, featuring a dedicated series of discussions on artificial intelligence for the first time as participants examine how to balance the opportunities of AI-driven innovation with the risks posed by the rapidly evolving technology.

The new track will explore how AI can be developed and deployed to foster innovation, strengthen resilience, and create new opportunities for growth, drawing on China’s experience as well as perspectives from Singapore and the broader region, according to the forum’s organizer.

The two-day forum is organized by Business China, a non-profit organization initiated by Singapore’s Founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew. It brings together business leaders, experts, government officials, and academics from China and Singapore to discuss economic, geopolitical, technological, and societal developments.

Held under the theme of “Strengthening Resilience, Rebuilding Trust,” this year’s forum comes amid heightened geopolitical and economic uncertainty, rapid technological change, and differing approaches to growth and governance. Discussions will examine how countries and businesses can navigate these shifts, adapt to disruption, and sustain the trust and practical cooperation needed for long-term growth.

The forum also comes as China enters its 15th Five-Year Plan period, covering this year through 2030, with innovation, industrial upgrading,  and domestic demand identified as key economic priorities. Against this backdrop, participants will explore how these developments and broader global shifts could shape opportunities for China, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, and the wider region.

“The global economy is no longer operating from a single playbook,” said Lee Yi Shyan, chairman of Business China. “For Singapore, China, and the region, resilience will depend not only on adapting to different systems and models, but also on building trust and finding practical ways to work together.

“The FCGF seeks to contribute to this by bringing together diverse perspectives and fostering dialogue on how we can navigate uncertainty, deepen understanding and identify opportunities for cooperation,” Lee added.

The AI track will run from 1 p.m. to 6 p.m. today, while the main forum is scheduled from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. tomorrow.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Connecting Innovation and Global Markets: Jeanne Wang on CanSinoBIO’s Next Stage of Growth
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 24-- Five years ago, Jeanne Wang transitioned from Chief Financial Officer to Chief Commercial Officer at CanSino Biologics (CanSinoBIO), a pioneering Chinese biotechnology company focused on vaccine innovation, following the company’s listings in Hong Kong and Shanghai. Over the past five years, she has played a leading role in shaping the company’s evolution from an R&D-focused biotech into a business with a growing commercial portfolio and an increasingly international footprint.

That evolution is becoming increasingly visible in CanSinoBIO’s financial and commercial performance. In the first half of 2026, the company reported revenue of RMB550 million, up 43.8% year on year, while overseas revenue reached RMB152 million.

For Jeanne Wang, the growth is not an overnight development, but the result of years of investment and preparation. “It is not a surprise,” she said. “It reflects the direction we have been committed to for years.”

Having been with CanSinoBIO for 15 years, Jeanne Wang has been part of its transformation from early-stage vaccine research and fundraising to public listings, scaled manufacturing, commercialization and international expansion. Looking ahead, she sees the company’s next stage as one defined by closer integration between innovation and the market.

She believes commercialization is about creating stronger connections between innovation, products and market needs. As CanSinoBIO advances its commercialization efforts, this approach is increasingly reflected in the expansion of its product portfolio.

Its quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine (MCV4) continues to contribute commercial revenue, while its 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV13i) has advanced in both domestic and overseas markets. The company is also extending its pertussis portfolio across different age groups. Its three-component diphtheria, tetanus and acellular pertussis vaccine (DT3cP) has been approved in China for infants, while its New Drug Application (NDA) for a five-component product (Td5cp) targeting adolescents and adults was accepted by China’s NMPA for review in August.

Meanwhile, the company has expanded the indicated age range of MCV4 and received approval for its adsorbed tetanus vaccine, adding further depth to its portfolio. For CanSinoBIO, however, expanding the portfolio is not simply about adding more products. The company is also seeking to leverage its five core technology platforms across different vaccine programs. Its DT3cP-Hib-MCV4 combination vaccine and recombinant polio vaccine currently under clinical development illustrate this approach.

The broader objective is to move from individual products toward greater platform synergies — from single vaccines to combination and multivalent products, and from pediatric immunization to a broader life-course portfolio.

This transformation is taking place alongside another major shift: the company’s internationalization. Chinese vaccine makers have accelerated their efforts to enter overseas markets in recent years, but international expansion involves more than securing regulatory approval and supplying products. Companies must navigate differences in disease burden, regulatory systems, immunization policies, healthcare financing, supply chains, manufacturing capabilities and commercial channels.

CanSinoBIO is therefore seeking to integrate domestic and overseas operations rather than treating international business as a separate track. The development of PCV13i in Indonesia offers an example. As one of Southeast Asia’s largest markets, Indonesia is expanding its capacity to meet growing immunization needs through domestic investment and procurement. CanSinoBIO has supplied the intermediate product for its PCV13i vaccine to the Indonesian partner, supporting subsequent local manufacturing and potential supply to the national immunization program.

For Jeanne Wang, the experience highlights an important principle for Chinese vaccine companies going global: there is no single model that works across markets. “The starting point is always the local needs,” she said, referring to factors including disease burden, regulatory requirements, immunization policies and market demand. Products and partnership models need to match those conditions.

In some emerging markets, she has observed that the interest of local partners goes beyond individual products. They are increasingly interested in technology platforms and in developing innovative vaccines through clinical studies involving local populations, to achieve regulatory approval in their own markets alongside other countries.

This points to a broader shift in the internationalization of Chinese vaccine companies — from exporting products to expanding technology, clinical development and industrial capabilities overseas.

For CanSinoBIO, that represents an extension of its commercialization strategy rather than a separate path outside the domestic business. The company is seeking to build a portfolio that can address different stages of the life course while developing partnerships that connect its technologies and products with local healthcare needs.

Jeanne Wang also sees opportunities for greater collaboration among China’s innovative biopharmaceutical companies as they expand internationally. In her view, if companies can build more effective cooperation around real market and public health needs — from products and technologies to supply chains and local partnerships — Chinese innovators could enter global markets in a more efficient and sustainable way.

For Jeanne Wang, the next phase is therefore more about finding ways for innovation to create value across different healthcare systems. After 15 years at CanSinoBIO, her perspective reflects not only the company’s shift from R&D toward commercialization, but also a broader question facing China’s innovative biopharmaceutical sector: how to connect domestic innovation more effectively with healthcare needs around the world.

data.title: Vocational Education Needs Stable Frameworks to Keep Pace With Tech Changes, Pearson Exec Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 23 -- Keeping pace with rapid technological changes and evolving skills requires stable standard frameworks, such as the Business and Technology Education Council qualifications, according to Freya Thomas Monk, Managing Director of Vocational Qualifications at UK education giant Pearson. 

“Technology changes every two days,” Monk told Yicai during BTEC Connect 2026 in Shanghai yesterday. The discussion took place as the 48th WorldSkills Competition was being held in the city, with 1,385 competitors from 68 countries and regions participating, both figures setting new records.

Changes in the competition's skills categories also reflect industrial transformation, from traditional skills, such as carpentry and bricklaying, to emerging fields like drone applications, digital media, and smart security.

Together with the Beijing Human Resource Service Industrial Association and a research group from Beijing Forestry University, Pearson yesterday released a report titled “Cultivation of International-oriented Skilled Talents and Industry-Education Integration” at the BTEC Connect 2026 conference in Shanghai. 

The report found that a growing gap is emerging between companies' talent requirements and existing training models, and the match rate between vocational college majors and industrial demand is about 65 percent.

Strengthening school-enterprise cooperation is an important way to bridge the gap between talent development and industrial demand, said Shen Zhiyu, Secretary General of the Beijing Human Resource Service Industrial Association. 

“We need to move beyond fragmented cooperation and build more sustainable partnerships that connect vocational education more closely with real workplace needs,” said Shen Zhiyu, secretary-general of the Beijing Human Resource Service Industrial Association. 

Companies update their equipment and production processes roughly every one to one and a half years, while vocational colleges often run training programs from three to five years prior, the report showed, identifying other shortcomings in English proficiency and cross-cultural adaptability.

"While technology changes rapidly, vocational education should be built on enduring skills and standards that can evolve alongside new developments," Monk pointed out.

Under the BTEC framework, technologies for specific industries can be adjusted as market conditions change, while the knowledge, skills, and competencies students acquire remain relatively stable, she explained. This lets educational institutions update teaching content based on industry practices without frequently changing the underlying qualification standards.

Keeping teachers up to date with technological changes is another challenge vocational education faces. The key is to ensure that teachers have the knowledge, tools, and technology needed to deliver instruction, while helping learners understand the impact of technology on their chosen industries, Monk said. “We must all focus on supporting the teachers and educators through this change.”

Beyond technical skills, companies are also placing more and more importance on workers' broader international capabilities, including adaptability, problem-solving, and cross-cultural collaboration, according to the report.

“I would love to see every young person confident that they have technical vocational skills plus the human skills of teamwork, problem-solving, and creativity, because together that is what will drive their success,” Monk noted.

Combining technical skills with transferable capabilities can help learners respond to changes in future working environments, she said, adding that international standards also need to be aligned with local industry requirements. “Standards and benchmarks only work and are useful if they really meet the needs of local employers and local economies.”

During BTEC Connect, Pearson also signed a memorandum of understanding with the Northern International Testing Centre (NITC) to deepen cooperation in areas including vocational skills certification, digital credentials, and international vocational education.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s Biwin Jumps on USD670 Million Plan to Expand Memory Packaging Capacity Amid AI Boom
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 23 -- Shares in Biwin Storage Technology soared by as much as 5.2 percent today after the Chinese provider of semiconductor memory solutions and advanced packaging and testing products said it will invest CNY4.5 billion (USD670 million) to build the third phase of its advanced memory packaging and testing facility in southern Guangdong province, as surging artificial intelligence computing demand drives growth in the memory market.

Biwin’s share price [SHA: 688525] closed up 2.5 percent at CNY222.69 (USD33.21) today. Earlier in the day it hit CNY228.56.

Biwin’s subsidiary Guangdong Xincheng Hanqi Semiconductor Technology will be responsible for the construction of Phase Three of a wafer-level advanced memory packaging and testing manufacturing project in the Dongguan Songshan Lake High-Tech Industrial Development Zone, the Shenzhen-based firm said yesterday, citing the investment agreement penned between Xincheng Hanqi and the zone’s management.

Xincheng Hanqi is the project company responsible for the construction and operation of Biwin’s Dongguan base in Guangdong province. Biwin holds a 68.27 percent stake, while four employee shareholding platforms collectively own 29.26 percent. The remaining approximately 2.47 percent of the shares are held by an external investor.

Biwen did not disclose the planned annual production capacity of Phase Three, nor did it provide details such as a construction timeline. It only said that the project will be constructed on land at the existing production base, and that the total investment is expected to be completed by the end of 2029.

Biwin announced plans in October 2023 to invest CNY3.1 billion (USD462.2 million) in the Dongguan base to build a wafer-level advanced memory packaging and testing manufacturing project in two phases. The newly announced third phase reflects the company’s latest decision to expand capacity in response to market demand.

Both Phases One and Two of the Dongguan base use 2.5D packaging technology, with a combined capacity of approximately 3,000 wafers per month, according to the firm’s latest update released yesterday. Phase One has entered the customer sampling, process validation, and small-scale trial production stages, while Phase Two is undergoing equipment installation and debugging.

Compared with conventional packaging, 2.5D advanced packaging shortens signal transmission paths, enabling higher bandwidth and lower latency. Advanced packaging also offers advantages in miniaturization, lightweight design, lower power consumption and greater functional integration, helping improve chip performance and supporting applications in emerging fields such as smart devices and high-performance computing.

Biwin said the new investment will help the company achieve breakthroughs in key technologies for advanced packaging and testing, enabling mass production of multi-chip system-in-package solutions and computing-memory integrated packages.

Biwin is primarily engaged in the research, design, packaging and testing of semiconductor memory products. Driven by strong demand from the expansion of AI applications, Biwin’s operating revenue quadrupled in the first half from a year earlier to CNY15.6 billion (USD2.3 billion). Net profit was CNY7.2 billion, compared with a net loss of CNY226 million (USD33.7 million) in the same period last year.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: CATL’s Hungary Plant Starts Trial Production of Battery Cells
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 23 -- Chinese power battery giant Contemporary Amperex Technology has said its new battery cell plant in Debrecen, Hungary has officially started trial production.

This phase aims to debug, optimize, and validate production equipment and manufacturing processes, in preparation for mass production, CATL said yesterday. The Debrecen facility is CATL’s second battery plant in Europe and its largest overseas manufacturing base.

Plans for the Debrecen plant were first unveiled in August 2022, including a total investment of about EUR7.34 billion (USD8.38 billion), a facility area of 221 hectares, and a planned total production capacity of 100 gigawatt-hours.

The plant started producing battery modules in the autumn of 2024, and the cumulative output has reached 537,000 sets, but the facility has been beset by increasing friction with authorities in the country and local concerns about the environmental impact.

Production was halted last month following a safety incident involving workers’ exposure to nickel, and the government of Hungary also announced that it would suspend preferential simplified licensing treatment for what it described as “illegal battery plants.”

In response, CATL stated that before the battery cell factory use license was approved, the Hungarian Hajdu-Bihor State Government Office had regularly conducted on-site inspections of the Debrecen factory and continued to follow up on issues that had previously caused concern to local residents. The regulatory authorities also confirmed that the company had completed all rectification work identified during the review for the permit.

In August, CATL obtained the factory use permit and the Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control permit, and started trial production of battery cells after completing all the legal prerequisites.

Operation at CATL’s first overseas plant in Thuringia, Germany began in early 2023, and the factory achieved profitability on a yearly basis for the first time in 2025. The Debrecen plant will serve leading European car firms such as Mercedes Benz, BMW, Stellantis, and Volkswagen, CATL said.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: [Exclusive] CAS Space, Guangzhou Lab Partner on Space Biomedicine to Co-Develop Space Pharma Payload
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 22 -- CAS Space Technology and Guangzhou Laboratory have teamed up on space biomedicine to jointly develop a space pharmaceutical payload, aiming to conduct crystallization experiments on protein and small molecule drugs and to accumulate a technical foundation for future orbital-level, long-term experiments, Yicai learned from exclusive sources.

Their medical payload will be used to research and develop new drugs for major diseases, such as lung cancer and cardiovascular diseases. It will take CAS Space’s Li Hong-2 reusable spacecraft to complete suborbital flight verification in the first quarter of next year to explore the development of new drugs in a microgravity environment and answer “questions of life” in space.

Space biomedicine uses the unique microgravity and special radiation environment in space to conduct biomedical research and preparation of drugs that are difficult or even impossible to achieve in ground laboratories. Its core advantages are growing higher-quality protein crystals to assist in the molecular design of new drugs, more realistic human disease models to improve drug screening, and quick stimulation of human degenerative diseases and search for therapeutic targets.

“Space biomedicine is not a new topic,” Wang Yingcheng, executive vice president of the CAS Space Technology Innovation Research Institute, told Yicai in an interview. “It was mainly research-oriented, but now has reached a critical point of industrialization”

The combination of commercial aerospace and biomedicine requires a high level of radiofrequency to support the research, development, manufacturing, and evolution of space biomedicine, and demands low costs for commercialization, Wang noted.

Compared with ground experiments, space biomedicine experiments cost more and are harder to reproduce and validate. The expansion of commercial aerospace production capacity has brought new development opportunities for the industrialization of this field.

The core objective of the cooperation with Guangzhou Lab is to jointly develop space pharmaceutical payloads, aiming to build the ability to conduct crystallization experiments on protein and small-molecule drugs and to accumulate a technical foundation for future orbital-level long-term experiments, Wang said.

Founded in 2021, Guangzhou Lab is led by Zhong Nanshan, an academician at the Chinese Academy of Engineering. It focuses on respiratory diseases and their prevention and control.

Guangzhou Lab is an important part of the national strategic scientific and technological strength and a core source of original innovation, major scientific and technological breakthroughs, and achievement transformation in biomedicine in Guangdong province. Its cooperation with CAS Space is mainly carried out by a team led by researcher Xu Qiang.

In the partnership, Guangzhou Lab raises scientific questions about drug crystallization, handles experimental plans, samples, ground controls, and result analysis, and translates mature biopharmaceutical automation functions and in-situ observation capabilities into payload requirements, Xu told Yicai in an interview. CAS Space is responsible for the space platform, environmental conditions, system interfaces, launch and return, and mission organization. They jointly conduct payload engineering design.

The global space pharmaceutical field is still in the early stage, with more scientific research projects than large-scale commercial products, Wang noted. Access, returns, costs, and regulatory mechanisms are still being improved. Several verifiable developments have emerged internationally, demonstrating scientific value and engineering feasibility, but the commercial value of specific drugs and tasks still needs verification.

CAS Space’s future layout in space biomedicine is to create a space-ground collaborative production environment and build a long-term, in-orbit manufacturing base from ground experiments to suborbital flights, low Earth orbit, and experimental modules, Yicai learned.

CAS Space is a leading commercial aerospace enterprise under the Chinese Academy of Sciences, mainly engaged in researching, developing, producing, and launching medium and large commercial carrier rockets. It is exploring new forms of the space economy, such as space manufacturing, space science experiments, and space tourism.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Xpeng-Backed Flying Car Giant Aridge Partners With UAE to Set Up Regulatory Sandbox
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 22 -- Aridge, the flying car company backed by Chinese new energy vehicle giant Xpeng Group, formerly known as Xpeng AeroHT, has reached a deal with officials of the United Arab Emirates to establish a regulatory cooperation mechanism for air traffic.

Aridge and the Emirate of Ras Al Khaimah agreed to jointly set up an air traffic regulatory sandbox platform under the UAE General Civil Aviation Authority to promote the airworthiness certification and commercialization of low-altitude flying products in the Middle East, the Guangzhou-based company announced on Sept. 20.

Aridge will leverage the regulatory sandbox mechanism to conduct systematic flight testing in typical scenarios in the Middle East, focusing on collecting data about the aircraft performance, including power performance, endurance, airspace adaptability, and operational safety risks, under special environmental conditions, such as high temperatures and sandstorms. The company aims to complete localized adaptation verification.

Moreover, Aridge will carry out specialized feasibility verification for commercial deployment in diverse application scenarios, including high-end tourism and sightseeing, urban short-distance air transit, emergency rescue operations, and offshore oil platform inspections.

Aridge was founded in 2013 as Huitian. Xpeng and its founder He Xiaopeng invested in the company in 2020. Aridge has developed the Land Aircraft Carrier, the world's first modular flying car that combines electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft with automobiles. It achieved mass production and roll-out in March and is expected to launch within the year.

There is no unified flying car sandbox system in the Chinese mainland, an analyst told Yicai. However, six cities -- Hefei, Hangzhou, Shenzhen, Suzhou, Chengdu, and Chongqing -- have approved eVTOL pilot programs, opening up market opportunities for commercial passenger flights, the person added.

By 2040, the Chinese and overseas eVTOL markets are expected to reach USD41 billion and USD184 billion, respectively, presenting significant market opportunities for manufacturers, according to a report released by Boston Consulting Group last year. As a global hub for luxury consumption, the Middle East is emerging as a potential market for passenger eVTOLs.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s Dunhuang Joins Forces With GOVY to Launch Low-Altitude Tourism Services
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 23 -- The Chinese city of Dunhuang is teaming up with low-altitude manned aircraft manufacturer GOVY Technology to integrate low-altitude transportation into tourism offerings in the municipality, which lies in the northwest of the country and is famed for its location along the ancient Silk Road and its Mogao Cave murals.

The tie-up will cover a range of applications, including shuttle services, scenic-area sightseeing and cultural performances, Dunhuang authorities said at the signing ceremony yesterday. In the initial phase, standardized low-altitude sightseeing experiences will be built at major Dunhuang attractions such as Crescent Spring, Yumenguan Pass and the Yardang National Geopark. The city plans to eventually establish a low-altitude transportation loop connecting major scenic spots with the urban area.

Cultural tourism is emerging as one of the most promising entry points for low-altitude services, as it offers clear opportunities for paid services and direct public engagement, said Su Qingpeng, founder of Guangzhou-based GOVY. China’s low-altitude tourism market was worth nearly CNY40 billion (USD6 billion) last year and is expected to exceed USD200 billion by 2030, he added.

In the first half, China’s low-altitude cultural tourism sector recorded over 12 million flights, more than double the figure for the same period last year, Su added.

GOVY was originally the flying-car research and development division of state-owned automaker GAC Group before being spun off as an independently operated company at the end of 2024. GOVY AirCab, its two-seat electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, is expected to receive its airworthiness certification and start mass production and deliveries by the end of this year.

Dunhuang boasts several advantages for developing low-altitude tourism, a local official said. There are around 26,000 square kilometers of airspace below 300 meters that are suitable for flying, which is 97 percent of the city’s area. The metropolis has more than 300 days of suitable flying conditions each year. Dunhuang also receives 24 million tourists and holds hundreds of major events a year, providing favorable conditions for developing new tourism offerings.

The two parties will also collaborate on cultural and creative products. This will include incorporating imagery from Dunhuang’s famous Flying Apsaras murals and elements of Silk Road culture into the exterior designs of flying cars and sightseeing routes, as well as jointly developing themed cultural and creative products. The aim is to create an integrated business model combining flight experiences with cultural consumption.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Kim Taylor
